stem: The value of C(10, 4) + C(10, 6) is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: C(10,4) = 210 and C(10,6) = 210 (by symmetry C(10,6)=C(10,4)), so their sum is 420.
Reading only C(10,4) = 210 and forgetting to add C(10,6), treating the sum as a single term.
C(11,4) = 330 and C(11,5) = 462; a student applying Pascal's rule incorrectly writes C(10,4)+C(10,5) = C(11,5) = 462 instead of using C(10,6) = C(10,4).
Computing P(10,4)/something or doubling 420 by treating two groups as ordered gives 840.

explanation: Use the symmetry property C(n,r) = C(n, n-r). Since 4+6 = 10 = n, we have C(10,6) = C(10,4) = 210. Therefore C(10,4) + C(10,6) = 210 + 210 = 420.

explanation_sections.punchline: Symmetry C(n,r) = C(n, n-r) makes C(10,6) = C(10,4), so the sum is simply 2 * 210 = 420.
explanation_sections.approach: Classify: evaluating sum of combinations. Apply symmetry: C(10,6) = C(10, 10-6) = C(10,4). Compute C(10,4) = (10*9*8*7)/(4*3*2*1) = 5040/24 = 210. Sum = 210 + 210 = 420.
explanation_sections.lesson: C(n,r) = C(n, n-r) is the symmetry identity; use it to avoid computing large factorials whenever r > n/2.
explanation_sections.timing: 35 seconds. The fastest path: recognize C(10,6)=C(10,4) by symmetry, double the single value.
